growth_story.headline: Malta grew on online gaming, tourism and foreign workers, but income per person rose more slowly than the economy as the population swelled.
growth_story.arc: Malta's income per person grew 5.5 percent a year in 1990–2000. It then slowed to 1.5 percent in 2001–2009. The IMF links that slowdown to shocks to tourism and chip-making from 2001, weaker trading partners, and old factories shrinking after trade barriers fell for EU entry. Growth picked up to 4.8 percent in 2010–2017, as online gaming, professional services and tourism expanded, new energy projects were built and workers arrived from abroad. In 2018–2025 it eased to 2.8 percent, with a fall of 5.6 percent in 2020 and a rebound of 12.8 percent in 2021. Over 2016–2025 income per person grew 3.4 percent a year, close to the 3.5 percent of the decade before, and in 2025 it was at its highest level yet.

threads.title: Shocks to chips and tourism
threads.text: The IMF traces the weak 2000s to shocks in tourism and chip-making from 2001, made worse by slower growth in Malta's main trading partners. Joining the EU removed old import levies, and makers of food and drink sold less while clothing factories lost ground faster.

threads.title: Services and energy remake growth
threads.text: In the 2010s Malta kept growing through the euro area crisis. The IMF credited strong home demand and big building projects, including a new gas terminal, a power plant switched to gas and a power cable to Sicily. Online gaming grew into a larger source of growth than construction.

threads.title: Energy prices held fixed
threads.text: When world energy prices jumped in 2022, the government froze the prices that homes and firms pay for power and fuel. Even so, inflation rose to 6.2 percent in 2022 and 5.1 percent in 2023, and income per person barely grew in 2022. The cost of the energy support has since fallen as world prices eased.

since_last_year.text: The IMF's latest review, published in February 2026, says growth slowed in 2025. It expects growth to settle at a slower pace as the inflow of workers moderates and gaming and tourism reach saturation. In the data, income per person grew 2.0 percent in 2025, down from 3.2 percent in 2024.

growth_story.tension: The IMF describes a decade of very fast growth, with income per person rising quickly since 2013. In the data, income per person grew 3.4 percent a year in 2016–2025, about the same as the 3.5 percent of the decade before. Much of the gap is people: the whole economy grew far faster because the population and workforce grew fast too. The IMF's income per person figure is also in US dollars, while the data here take out price changes.
